I assume a partial recovery toward the pre-2023 range of roughly 19-24% before impairments, held back by higher depreciation and a weaker asset mix.

rev_growth.why: Year 1 (FY2026) is up modestly because nine-month revenue is above last year, with Q4 lower after the sales. Year 2 falls because the $545 million of 2026 sales is fully out of the base, then leasing and mark-to-market gains bring low growth. Year 1 revenue of about $498 million assumes Q4 near $117 million.

terminal_growth.why: This is a mature, shrinking-to-stable office portfolio facing structural pressure on space demand, so long-run growth sits below the 3.75% anchor.

debt_level_representative.why: Debt has fallen since the base year through asset sales (Net Debt/EBITDA 7.6x against 9.0x the prior quarter), but the base-year total debt of $2,556.9 million is higher than the current level and the credit facility matures December 31, 2026.

situation.margin_position: The GAAP operating margin of 5.5% in 2025 is depressed by a $63.4 million impairment and by high property costs and depreciation on a mostly office portfolio. Nine-month 2026 margin before gains and impairments is about 14%, and property operating expenses are rising faster than revenue. The margin is structurally low for a REIT and is not a cyclical trough.

tax_rate_representative.why: As a REIT it pays almost no income tax (about 0.2% in the filed record), and the nine-month provision was only $67 thousand.

situation.why: The 2025 base year carries large impairments, and the portfolio has since shrunk by more than $500 million of sales, so 2025 revenue and costs overstate the go-forward asset base. Nine-month 2026 revenue was 381,562 against 363,504, but most of the sold properties leave the revenue base from Q4 2026 onward. Year 2 revenue should therefore drop before leasing growth resumes.

loss_record.explanation: Operations are profitable before interest: nine-month 2026 operating income is $68.1 million, and about $12.3 million even without the $55.8 million disposition gain. Impairments are also large, but they recur every year (2024 and 2025), so they do not explain the thin record as well as interest does.
